cards.title: A recommendation engine for the entertainment space, built into a…
cards.one_line: A recommendation engine for the entertainment space, built into a social app and matched to your taste. Picked for you based on other people’s metrics that are similar to you - the bar playing your music, a comedy show starting in 40 minutes with jokes you laugh at, the rooftop that’s busy tonight with the same crowd you vibe with. Revenue comes from promoted event listings and anonymized audience insights sold to venues, and a subscription that unlocks perks. Log your experiences, connect with others, the possibilities are endless.

cards.title: I want to build an AI-powered Sports Performance Agent for…
cards.one_line: I want to build an AI-powered Sports Performance Agent for **Backfield**, our athlete movement intelligence platform, and pilot it with real athletes and coaches at the Los Gatos Performance & Movement Lab. The agent will transform biomechanical data from video-based motion capture (OpenCap), force plates, velocity-based training sensors, and GPS into actionable performance insights. Rather than requiring coaches to interpret complex datasets, athletes and trainers can ask questions like, “What is limiting my sprint performance?”, “Has my movement improved since my last assessment?”, or “What should I focus on in my next training session?” **HarnessRouter** would orchestrate specialized AI agents for movement analysis, performance interpretation, and personalized recommendations, optimizing model selection, tool execution, and inference costs. Our goal during the five-day hackathon is to launch a working agent, onboard real athletes and coaches, and demonstrate measurable customer adoption. **Target users:** High school and collegiate athletes, strength and conditioning coaches, sports performance facilities, and physical therapists.

cards.title: I am a physician with a background in Information Systems and AI…
cards.one_line: I am a physician with a background in Information Systems and AI, currently pursuing a DBA in Information Technology Management at Westcliff University. In 2026, I participated individually in the Menlo College Startup Pitch Competition. My Smart Urban Care Network (SUCN) project reached the finals and received a prize. I am also developing an AI-powered breast cancer prevention app focused on education, risk assessment, early detection support, and timely medical follow-up. I would like to use AI to improve preventive healthcare and community safety, especially for vulnerable populations. I hope to collaborate with AI developers to build practical prototypes that connect people with appropriate care and services while keeping important decisions under human oversight.

cards.title: Kashtree (kashtree.tech), an existing early-stage AI invoice-to-cash…
cards.one_line: Kashtree (kashtree.tech), an existing early-stage AI invoice-to-cash app for Latino contractors in Florida (remodeling, HVAC, cleaning) who lose money to unpaid invoices and scattered paperwork. During build week I'll build a NEW collections agent on HarnessRouter: it reads photos of invoices, receipts and job docs, builds the job file, drafts bilingual (EN/ES) payment reminders for the owner's approval, and routes each task to the cheapest harness x model that does it well, compared in Arena. Goal: paying contractors using the agent during the week. Software engineer with a Master's in AI; based in Colombia but Actually visiting Miami Florida, building remotely.

cards.title: I’d like to build a code quality evaluation agent that helps…
cards.one_line: I’d like to build a code quality evaluation agent that helps engineering teams measure and build trust in AI-generated code, especially in mature codebases where regressions and maintenance costs matter. The core feature would be quantitative, repository-aware quality scoring across correctness, maintainability, architectural consistency, test coverage, and performance. Each score would be backed by concrete evidence, with clear visibility into what was verified and what remains uncertain. I’d use HarnessRouter to coordinate analysis and validation agents, combining code review with automated checks and targeted tests. Teams could use the results to evaluate pull requests, compare coding agents, and track quality over time. For the hackathon, I’d start with a public repository and validate the scoring against historical changes and known defects.
